brief.headline: Kirillovka resort strike and mass drone barrage dominate
brief.lead: Pro-Kremlin channels converged on a Ukrainian strike on the Russian-held Kirillovka resort (claimed 8–12 dead, including children) and a large overnight drone barrage on Russian regions, while amplifying Russian strikes on Black Sea ports and a Ukrainian hit on an Iranian vessel in the Caspian. Tone was split: triumphant on strikes into Ukraine, aggrieved on attacks against Russia.

developments.title: Channels blame Ukraine for deadly Kirillovka resort strike
developments.body: Multiple channels claimed a Ukrainian drone/strike on the Alyeon resort in Kirillovka (Russian-held Zaporizhzhia) killed 8–12 civilians including two to four children and wounded up to 19, framing it as deliberate terrorism against non-military targets. Death tolls varied by channel (8, 11, 12) — unconfirmed.

developments.title: Large overnight Ukrainian drone barrage claimed across Russian regions
developments.body: Channels cited 250+ Ukrainian drones with 328 reportedly shot down (MoD-style figures), power cuts in Crimea, five wounded in Rostov, strikes on Belgorod residential areas, and repeated attacks on Wildberries logistics hubs in St. Petersburg and Crimea framed as 'economic terror.' Figures unconfirmed.

developments.title: Ukrainian strike on Iranian Caspian vessel draws Tehran protest
developments.body: Several channels reported a Ukrainian strike on an Iranian merchant ship in the Caspian Sea killing an Iranian sailor, with Iran summoning Ukraine's charge d'affaires and warning of retaliation. Framed as Kyiv provoking Iran to court Trump — unconfirmed.

developments.title: Russian strikes hit Black Sea ports and energy grid
developments.body: Channels touted Russian MoD-reported strikes on Odesa, Mykolaiv and Chornomorsk ports (claiming four merchant vessels and Swedish CB90 boats hit), plus Geran drones destroying Chernihiv substations with claimed cascading blackouts affecting 100,000+. Damage claims unverified.

developments.title: West coverage sours on NATO command and Trump-Iran messaging
developments.body: Rybar and Two Majors highlighted a British general assuming command of the Multinational Force Ukraine in Paris, Turkey's continued F-35 exclusion over S-400s, and skepticism toward Trump's claim that Putin promised not to arm Iran while the US keeps supplying Ukraine via NATO.

developments.title: Upbeat Russia-internal content on hardware and youth militarism
developments.body: Positive posts featured the Admiral Nakhimov nuclear cruiser completing sea trials, the Zarnitsa 2.0 military-patriotic youth competition, and a WarGonzo documentary series praising a Hyacinth-S artillery crew — driving a notable positive swing in Russia-internal sentiment.

narrative_watch.title: 'Ukraine targets civilians' terrorism framing
narrative_watch.body: The Kirillovka casualties are being packaged as deliberate terrorism against a resort, with shifting death tolls used to maximize outrage — a recurring civilian-victim frame worth tracking.

narrative_watch.title: 'Economic terror' against Russian retail
narrative_watch.body: Channels reframe Ukrainian drone hits on Wildberries logistics hubs as an economic-warfare campaign against Russian civilian commerce rather than military targets.

narrative_watch.title: Zelensky 'courting Trump via Iran'
narrative_watch.body: Rybar advances the claim that Kyiv struck Iranian-linked Caspian targets specifically to align with Trump's anti-Iran rhetoric — a geopolitical wedge narrative.

mood_lines.text: Uniformly triumphant (net +100); channels tout port, warehouse and energy strikes across Odesa, Mykolaiv, Zaporizhzhia and Chernihiv.
Uniformly aggrieved (net -100), centered on Kirillovka casualties, the drone barrage, Wildberries hits and the Iranian vessel incident.
Turned sharply negative (net -18, down 42); NATO command handover and distrust of Trump's Iran assurances drive frustration.
Notably more positive (net +60, up 48) on naval hardware, youth militarism and artillery praise, despite one abandoned-border-town lament.
Sparse but confident; claims of weekly settlement gains near Hulyaipole and along the Seversky Donets.
Small volume aimed outward at Ukrainian command war crimes and Kharkiv corruption; no domestic self-criticism.

flag_texts.title: West & NATO sentiment drops 42 points
flag_texts.body: West/NATO net sentiment fell to -18 as channels reacted negatively to a British general taking command of the Multinational Force Ukraine and to Trump's claim that Putin promised not to arm Iran while Washington keeps supplying Ukraine.

flag_texts.title: Russia-internal sentiment jumps 48 points
flag_texts.body: Russia-internal net rose to +60, lifted by upbeat coverage of the Admiral Nakhimov cruiser's sea trials, the Zarnitsa 2.0 youth military competition, and a laudatory documentary series on a Hyacinth-S artillery crew.

flag_texts.title: Mobilisation and Putin criticism stay silent
flag_texts.body: Watchlist topics 'Mobilisation rumours' and 'Criticism of Putin' had no substantive posts today; mobilisation-adjacent content was limited to positive youth-militarism framing (Zarnitsa 2.0).
